inventory.visualPurpose: Differentiation of T cells — the four-column pathway diagram
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Four vertical columns (Bone marrow → Thymus → Lymph node → Peripheral blood): a T-cell precursor leaves the bone marrow, enters the thymus (an anatomical lobed illustration with Cortex and Medulla leader labels) as a double-positive CD4+ CD8+ thymocyte, passes positive selection (+ icon, cortex) and negative selection (− icon, medulla), exits as CD8+ Cytotoxic (upper path) or CD4+ Helper (lower path); the Helper cell fans into Th1 / Th2 / Th17 / Treg circles, each arrow labeled with promoting (+) and inhibiting (−) cytokines (Th1: +IFN-γ, IL-12 / −IL-4, IL-10; Th2: +IL-2, IL-4 / −IFN-γ; Th17: +TGF-β, IL-1, IL-6 / −IFN-γ, IL-4; Treg: +TGF-β, IL-2 / −IL-6), feeding the Secretes/Function table at right.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Two-column table (Secretes / Function) with four rows: Th1 (IFN-γ, IL-2 / Activate macrophages and cytotoxic T cells), Th2 (IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-10, IL-13 / Activate eosinophils, ↑IgE), Th17 (IL-17, IL-21, IL-22 / Induce neutrophilic infiltration), Treg (TGF-β, IL-10, IL-35 / Prevent autoimmunity (maintain tolerance)).
